claims.text: Adolescents perceive social media as a threat to mental wellbeing.
Adolescents believe social media causes mood and anxiety disorders for some peers.
Adolescents view social media as a platform for cyberbullying.
Adolescents frame the use of social media as a form of addiction.

evidence.description: Thematic analysis suggested that adolescents perceived social media as a threat to mental wellbeing.
Thematic analysis identified that social media was believed to cause mood and anxiety disorders for some adolescents.
Thematic analysis identified that social media was viewed as a platform for cyberbullying.
Thematic analysis identified that the use of social media itself was often framed as a kind of 'addiction'.

methodologies.name: Focus group thematic analysis
methodologies.description: Conducting six focus groups over 3 months with adolescents to evaluate perceptions of social media through thematic analysis.
datasets: 54 adolescents aged 11-18 years recruited from schools in Leicester and London (UK)

limitations.text: There is a dearth of empirical research into how adolescents themselves perceive social media, especially as a knowledge resource, or how they draw upon wider social and media discourses.

future_work.text: Targeting and utilizing social media for promoting mental wellbeing among adolescents.
Educating youth to manage the possible deleterious effects of social media.
